task.title: Add 'Extension Points' sections to system docs
task.description: Add 'Extension Points' sections to system documentation that guide developers (human and LLM) on how to extend the system with new components.
task.problem:
System docs describe architecture well but don't guide how to extend the system. LLMs (and humans) must reverse-engineer extension patterns from existing code.
Evidence: Task 015 had to discover global-actions-view.capability.ts as a template via exploration. This knowledge could be baked into the doc instead.
Pattern docs already have 'When to Use' and checklists (good), but system docs like systems/vscode-extension describe layers without explaining 'add a new capability by...'.
task.value:
Faster, more consistent implementations. The doc becomes a 'how to add new X' guide, not just 'what X is'.
Benefits: - LLMs can implement new features faster with explicit guidance - Humans get onboarding documentation for extending the system - Reduces errors from reverse-engineering patterns incorrectly - Codifies tribal knowledge that would otherwise be lost
task.acceptance-criteria:
Given a system doc like systems/vscode-extension And it describes a component type (capability, orchestrator, etc.) When the doc is read by a developer or LLM Then it includes an 'Adding a new X' section with: - Template file to copy (e.g., "Copy global-actions-view.capability.ts") - Checklist of files to modify (e.g., "Register in extension.ts, add to package.json contributes") - Common pitfalls specific to that extension (e.g., "Don't forget to dispose subscriptions")
Given multiple component types in a system doc When extension points are documented Then each component type has its own 'Adding a new X' subsection
Given the systems/vscode-extension doc When extension points are added Then it covers at minimum: capabilities, orchestrators, and tree providers
